# HeritageGraph Ontology

> HeritageGraph is an event-centric OWL ontology for describing Nepalese living heritage — its tangible objects, sacred places, deities, rituals, festivals, and the communities and institutions (notably the *Guthi*) that sustain them. Rather than attaching facts directly to objects, the model represents history as a web of events (production, ritual, custody transfer, documentation) so that spatial, temporal, and participatory relationships can be queried and reasoned over. Every assertion can carry its provenance and epistemic standing, allowing competing or multi-vocal sources to coexist. The 

- Ontology IRI: https://cair-nepal.org/heritagegraph/ontology
- Namespace: https://cair-nepal.org/heritagegraph/ (prefix `hg:`)
- Version: 1.0.1
- License: CC BY 4.0
- Contents: 108 classes, 179 object properties, 45 datatype properties, 39 annotation properties, 10 concept schemes, 62 concepts

Terms are identified by IRI; use the CURIEs and labels below when writing SPARQL or RDF.

## Machine-readable

- [ontology.json](https://cairnepal.github.io/heritagegraphontology/ontology.json): all terms as JSON (IRI, label, definition, hierarchy, domain/range)
- [llms-full.txt](https://cairnepal.github.io/heritagegraphontology/llms-full.txt): the complete documentation as one Markdown file
- [Turtle](https://cairnepal.github.io/heritagegraphontology/ontology.ttl): the ontology source (text/turtle)
- [RDF/XML](https://cairnepal.github.io/heritagegraphontology/ontology.owl): the ontology source (application/rdf+xml)
- [JSON-LD](https://cairnepal.github.io/heritagegraphontology/ontology.jsonld): the ontology source (application/ld+json)
- [N-Triples](https://cairnepal.github.io/heritagegraphontology/ontology.nt): the ontology source (application/n-triples)
